lens: all three in turn (learning-scientist, examiner, learner-advocate)
scope_note: Teaching quality only; no factual checking (knowledge-only mode). Walked every node of module.json (S1.hook to END), read sim/*.md and sim/*.report.json, and checked report texts against the sim paths.

segments.reason: Strong hook: S1.hook is a real probe with confidence, S1.retest_route re-asks TR1 in a new form, S1.tim_probe tests the 'relatively' qualifier. Flaws: S1.hook femoral option is dominated by the stem's vessel framing, and S1.hook_t1 'Try again' replays the identical stem.

Weakest trap work: S2.tri_probe2 offers only two real options; 'Show me why' on S2.tri_t2a, S2.tri_t2b, S2.tri_t2c, S2.conj_t28a, S2.conj_t28b and S2.pic_t23a/b jumps to the next probe with no explanation; S2.tri_t2b is a one-line verdict with no reason; S2.tri_help gives away two of three options. Good: S2.pic_probe and S2.cause_predict tie cause and descent to the right sac.

Good predict-then-show: S3.predict (TR21), S3.occl_v and S3.lap (TR1 in clinical form), S3.tr40 (TR40). Flaws: S3.route is a two-option binary probe; S3.wall2 re-asks S3.wall's fact immediately; S3.contrast offers four long options each bundling three claims.

Telegraphed and leaky: S4.a_probe's key 'Femoral hernia of the groin' is the only option containing 'groin'; S4.f_probe's 'Strangulated direct' is dominated; S4.c1_probe's umbilical option is dominated; retry-only hints S4.a_hint, S4.b_hint, S4.c2_hint, S4.d1_hint, S4.d3_hint and S4.f_hint offer no escape to the answer; S4.d2_probe is repeated verbatim in S5.taxis_why. Strong: S4.f_probe case with the scope word, S4.d4_probe.

Best refutation writing in the module: 'Tempting: X' then the wrong model refuted, in S5.child_t1, S5.adult_t1, S5.adult_t2, S5.tri_t1, S5.tdef_t1, S5.tmesh_t1. Flaws: S5.tri is a binary probe; S5.taxis_why repeats S4.d2_probe; retry-only hints S5.emerg_hint, S5.child_hint, S5.lap_hint, S5.occ_hint, S5.tdef_hint; S5.ex2 packs four steps into one stem.

Good fresh-form retests (S6.p2 to S6.p6, S6.p9 to S6.p12, cold probes S6.p7 to S6.p12), but S6.p1 says 'the last six give no hints' while offering a hint, S6.p7's key is the only option without 'laparoscopic team available', S6.p4 is an odd-one-out key, and the 12-probe run feels padded (sim walks of 102 and 220 steps).

best_parts: node S1.hook: opens with a real exam stem, asks for a first instinct, traps TR1 and TR40 are plausible; the wrong answer leads to S1.hook_t1 with a sure_note.
node S1.retest_route: the same TR1 rule re-tested in a different form (position statement, not a stem), which is the delayed-retest pattern the contract asks for.
node S5.child_t1 and S5.tri_t1: 'Tempting: ...' names the wrong model, then refutes it with the claim, then offers 'Show me the answer'. Copy this pattern into S2.tri_t2b and S2.conj_t28a.
node S5.adult_t2: names the older PYQ key and the current standard side by side and asks which the stem wants. Good for TR17 and the examiner lens.
node S4.f_probe: vignette (painful groin lump, vomiting) with the scope word deciding the answer; TR9 and TR8 options are each a named wrong model.
node S3.predict: predict-then-show with a confidence tick on TR21 and a hint that names the mechanism without giving the answer.
node S6.p3: TR21 re-tested as a two-patient contrast with no hint; a fresh surface, which is what the report's fell_open text asks for.
node S6.p11: triangle of doom versus pain tested as a surgeon's tack location, with both boundary errors as separate options.
flaws: S6.p1: text says 'the last six give no hints' but the node offers 'Not sure, give me a hint' (S6.p1h); the same promise is broken for S6.p2 to S6.p6, which all offer hints.
S2.tri_probe2: only two real options (superficial ring, lateral rectus border) plus hint; too few distractors for a three-option trap map (conjoint tendon was planned as a partial).
S2.tri_t2b: 'The deep ring is not the triangle's lower edge.' is a one-line verdict with no why-tempting or refutation; its 'Show me why' goes to S2.tri_probe2 and explains nothing.

S2.tri_t2a, S2.tri_t2c, S2.conj_t28a, S2.conj_t28b, S2.pic_t23a, S2.pic_t23b: 'Show me why' routes to another probe (S2.tri_probe2, S2.conj_probe, S2.cause_predict, S2.final_probe), so the 'why' button never explains the wrong model.
S2.tri_help: 'one is a ring you pass through and one is an old base' removes two options, so the hint is the answer; a learner gets a free correct key.
S4.a_probe: the key 'Femoral hernia of the groin' is the only option containing 'groin', which is the stem's scope word; the key is findable by form (DP1).
S4.f_probe: 'Strangulated direct inguinal hernia' (TR8) is dominated for most learners because the indirect option is the commoner trap; a distractor nobody picks diagnoses nothing.
S4.c1_probe: 'Umbilical hernia' (partial) is dominated by femoral; the probe has no hint and no 'Not sure' option, so it is the one cold probe with no help.

S4.a_hint, S4.b_hint, S4.c2_hint, S4.d1_hint, S4.d3_hint, S4.f_hint, S5.emerg_hint, S5.child_hint, S5.nerve_hint, S5.lfcn_hint, S5.tri_hint, S5.occ_hint, S5.lap_hint, S5.tdef_hint, S5.taxis_why_hint, S5.ex2_hint, S6.p1h, S6.p3h, S6.p4h, S6.p5h, S6.p6h: hint offers only 'Try again', so a learner who does not know can only guess again; the hint ladder dead-ends (R5).

S4.d2_probe and S5.taxis_why: the same stem ('Why is forceful reduction avoided') with near-identical options, about 30 nodes apart; this is a repeat in the same form, not the different form the contract requires.
S5.tri: two options (pain correct, doom trap) plus hint; a coin-flip with no third distractor.
S3.route: two options (indirect lateral correct, direct medial trap); the mirror-image pair makes the key guessable from the question's 'enters through the deep ring'.
S3.wall2: re-asks the conjoint-tendon fact one node after S3.wall with the same answer; no spacing.
S3.contrast: four options, each bundling three claims (wall or cause, shape, finger test); a learner who knows one part cannot isolate which part the trap changed.

S6.p7: the key ('open-only surgeon') is the only option without 'laparoscopic team available' and the 'woman' detail is irrelevant; both traps share the same surface phrase, so the key is found by elimination of form.
S6.p4: two of three options begin 'The huge direct one'; the odd one out ('The small indirect one') is the key, a telegraphed structure.
S5.ex2: four numbered steps in one stem; 'one step is wrong' plus four claims asks the learner to hold the whole list (R4).

Report pace.fast_lane text: 'You earned the fast lane by answering the diagnostic correctly and sure' is wrong for any learner who skipped a lesson while guessing (sim guesser skipped at S4.a_ok and tapped Guessing throughout). The wording rule in report.md requires naming the skip and pointing to its cards.

Report help.hints_heavy text: 'You opened many hints' counts 'Show me the answer' reveals as hints (sim guesser: 0 hints, 16 reveals). The rule says the text must say 'asked for hints or explanations'.

Report strong path: pace.fast_lane does not name the four skipped lessons (S1.hook_ok, S2.route_predict, S3.start_ok, S4.a_ok) or the cards that cover them, so the learner who skipped is not told where the material is.

Report traps: confident-error traps (misconceived sim: 19 traps fell into under Sure) appear in the trap texts with no 'you were sure' marker, and card_order stays in the default 0 to 14 order, so the confident-errors-first rule seems not applied.

Coverage: objective O6 includes 'sliding contents' and the O6 gap text introduces 'a left sliding hernia most often contains sigmoid colon', but no probe teaches or tests sliding; O11's Richter and Maydl appear only in report text, not in any node.

Length and repetition: sim walks ran 102 steps (strong) and 220 steps (guesser, cut at the cap); the duplicated tests (S3.wall/wall2, S4.d3/S5.occ, S5.nerve/S5.lfcn/S6.p10, S5.adult/S5.ex2/S6.p8) cost time without new information.

novice.note: Headline weak, gap and shaky texts match the path, trap texts name the wrong model and the repair, hints and cold counts are right; next steps are clear.

misconceived.note: Calibration overconfident and trap texts are accurate, but the 19 Sure errors carry no 'you were sure' marker and card_order is unchanged, so the learner is not told which errors were confident.

strong.note: Headline strong and calibrated are right; the fast-lane text credits the diagnostic but does not name the four skipped lessons or where their cards are.

guesser.note: Says 'You opened many hints' (0 hints, 16 reveals) and 'You earned the fast lane by answering the diagnostic correctly and sure' (guessed throughout, skipped at S4.a_ok). Direction of weak areas is right, but two sentences misdescribe the path.

merge_ideas: S2 takes S5's 'Tempting: X' then refute pattern (S5.child_t1) in S2.tri_t2b and S2.conj_t28a, and points 'Show me why' at a real explanation node rather than the next probe.
S2.tri_probe2 gets the planned third distractor (conjoint tendon, partial) so it is a three-way probe, matching S2.tri_probe.
Every retry-only hint becomes the S3 pattern: hint, then 'Show me the answer' (agency) to the explanation node, so no probe dead-ends in a guess loop.
S5.taxis_why is recast as a case (which step to take first in a patient with dead-looking bowel) so the re-test is a different form from S4.d2_probe.
S4.a_probe and S6.p7 remove the form tells: put 'groin' in a distractor too, and give every option the same qualifier structure.

The report: pace.fast_lane splits into 'skipped' (names the lessons and cards, never 'earned') and 'earned' (diagnostic correct and Sure); help.hints_heavy says 'hints or explanations'; confident-error trap texts get the 'you were sure' marker and go first.
S6.p1 drops 'the last six give no hints' or the S6.p1 hint is removed so the promise holds; S6.p2 to S6.p6 keep their hints and the sentence is made true by naming the cold probes (S6.p7 onward).
